questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: You want one query over the KubePodInventory and ContainerLog tables to look for error statuses. Which operator combines rows from several tables?

options.text: union
mv-expand
join kind=inner
render

questions.explanation: union returns all rows from the listed tables in a single result, which suits searching across tables. join matches rows on keys, mv-expand expands arrays into rows, and render visualizes results.
questions.source_title: KQL quick reference

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: A column holds an array of sample times per session, and you need one row per sample. Which operator should you use?

options.text: mv-expand
extend
summarize
top

questions.explanation: mv-expand expands a dynamic array or property bag into multiple rows, one per element, as in the sample that charts concurrent sessions. Because the expanded values are dynamic, you often convert them with functions like todatetime before binning.

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: customDimensions in customEvents contains a JSON property TenantId. How do you group events by it?

options.text: project TenantId
extend tenant = tostring(customDimensions.TenantId) | summarize count() by tenant
summarize count() by customDimensions
where customDimensions == TenantId

questions.explanation: customDimensions is a dynamic column, so you access the property and convert it with tostring before grouping (parse_json is needed only when the value is stored as a string). Grouping by the whole bag treats every combination as different, and TenantId isn't a top-level column.

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: You need requests that took longer than 3 seconds together with the slow dependency calls made during the same operation. Which join key should you use between requests and dependencies?

options.text: timestamp
cloud_RoleName
operation_Id
itemCount

questions.explanation: All telemetry in one distributed operation shares operation_Id, so joining requests and dependencies on it pairs each request with the calls it made. Timestamps rarely match exactly, role name groups by service rather than by operation, and itemCount relates to sampling.

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: You chart hail events per day for three states and want each state in its own panel instead of overlapping lines. Which render option does this?

options.text: render timechart with (ysplit=panels)
render table
render timechart with (kind=stacked) only
render piechart

questions.explanation: ysplit=panels draws each series in its own panel of the time chart. A pie chart can't show time, kind=stacked stacks the series in one chart, and table shows rows rather than a chart.
questions.source_title: Time chart visualization (KQL)

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: You join StormEvents (column State) with PopulationData, whose matching column is named StateName. How do you write the join condition?

options.text: Rename isn't possible; the columns must have the same name
join kind=innerunique PopulationData on $left.State == $right.StateName
join PopulationData on State, StateName
join PopulationData where State = StateName

questions.explanation: When key columns have different names, KQL uses $left and $right to qualify them in the on clause. A comma-separated list means two keys that exist on both sides, where isn't join syntax, and you can also rename with project if you prefer.
questions.source_title: Tutorial: Join data from multiple tables (KQL)

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: In one summarize, you need both the total number of requests and the number that failed per hour. Which aggregation helps?

options.text: summarize sum(success) by bin(timestamp, 1h)
where success == false | summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 1h)
summarize count() by success, bin(timestamp, 1h) is the only way
summarize total = count(), failed = countif(success == false) by bin(timestamp, 1h)

questions.explanation: countif counts only rows where the predicate is true, so you can compute totals and failures side by side in one pass. Grouping by success splits the data into separate rows, summing a boolean isn't how you count failures, and filtering first loses the total.
questions.source_title: Tutorial: Use aggregation functions in KQL

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: For each computer, you need only its most recent heartbeat row with all columns. Which aggregation does this?

options.text: top 1 by TimeGenerated
distinct Computer
summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Computer
summarize max(TimeGenerated) by Computer

questions.explanation: arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) returns, for each group, the row with the largest TimeGenerated including all its columns. max returns only the timestamp, top 1 returns a single row overall, and distinct returns only computer names.

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: You want the log lines of a container app that mention errors, with the time, app name, revision, and message. Which query targets the right Container Apps table?

options.text: ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL | project TimeGenerated, ContainerAppName_s, RevisionName_s, Log_s | where Log_s contains "error"
ContainerLogV2 | where PodName contains "app"
AzureActivity | where Level == "Error"
AppRequests | where Success == false

questions.explanation: Container Apps writes stdout and stderr to ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL, with columns such as ContainerAppName_s, RevisionName_s, and Log_s, as in Microsoft's sample. AppRequests holds request telemetry, ContainerLogV2 holds AKS logs, and AzureActivity holds management events.

questions.stem: You built a daily time series of billable usage with make-series and want to flag unusual days automatically. Which KQL capability fits?

options.text: The distinct operator
render barchart
Series functions such as series_decompose_anomalies applied to the time series
A join with the Heartbeat table

questions.explanation: KQL includes time series analysis functions that decompose a series into baseline, seasonal, trend, and residual components and detect anomalies, as shown in the Azure Monitor anomaly detection tutorial. Rendering, distinct, or joins don't detect anomalies.

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: Which statement about bin() in KQL is correct?

options.text: It sorts rows by time
It rounds values down to multiples of a given size, so summarize ... by bin(timestamp, 1h) groups rows into hourly buckets
It converts strings to datetimes
It removes null values

questions.explanation: bin(value, roundTo) rounds values into fixed-size buckets, and combined with summarize it groups results by time intervals such as 5m, 1h, or 1d. It doesn't drop nulls, sort, or parse strings.

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: You need a list of the unique combinations of event name and session ID in AppEvents. Which operator returns them?

options.text: order by Name
summarize count()
take 100
distinct Name, SessionId

questions.explanation: distinct returns one row for each unique combination of the listed columns. summarize count() without by returns one total, take returns arbitrary rows, and order by only sorts.
questions.source_title: KQL quick reference

questions.skill_name: Write KQL queries to analyze logs and metrics
questions.stem: A query returns millions of rows and runs slowly. Which change usually helps the most?

options.text: Add render at the start of the query
Join every table first and filter at the end
Use contains instead of has
Filter early with where clauses, especially on time (for example where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)), before joins and aggregations

questions.explanation: Reducing data as early as possible, starting with a time filter, means later operators like join and summarize process far fewer rows. render must be last, contains is usually slower than has, and filtering after joins makes the joins process unneeded rows.
